clue.text: One who believes in doing things the right way

definitions.text: One who believes in doing things the right way

parts.words: One who believes in doing things the right way
parts.note: the right way reads as correct conduct, but it means the political right, so this is a follower of the right-wing party

explanation.definitionFit: A Tory supporter favours the political right, which is the 'right way' in a party sense.

clue.text: Strange people might end scrap

parts.note: strange means odd
men are people

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word might

explanation.surface: Weird folk could put a stop to a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight, but here it is a leftover piece; 'end' takes the T from 'might'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a leftover piece of material, as is a remnant left after cutting.

clue.text: Celebrity autograph? Everybody has one

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
to autograph is to sign; as a noun a sign is a mark of one's name

explanation.surface: A famous person's signature is something every fan seems to collect.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone is born under one of the twelve zodiac constellations, so each person has a birth sign.

clue.text: Travel through the Kalahari Desert

indicators.note: through tells us the letters run across the two words Kalahari Desert, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A journey across the sands of southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey on a horse or in a vehicle is to travel, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Give notice to department secretary

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a Secretary of State heads a government department, as a minister does

explanation.surface: Hand in your notice to the head of the department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give notice' looks like resigning, but 'Give' alone is the definition, as in giving a dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense medicine or justice is to give it out formally.

clue.text: Not reactionary

parts.note: reads as politically progressive, but means chemically unwilling to take part in reactions

explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas is chemically unreactive, showing no tendency to react with other substances.

clue.text: Chaos of hospital department in poor condition

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
ropy is British slang for in poor condition

explanation.surface: A badly run-down hospital ward is in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: ROPY is informal British English for shabby or unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics the measure of disorder in a system is a kind of chaos.

clue.text: Full of energy and cheeky, like tandem-rider of note

parts.note: fresh can mean impertinent or cheeky
like means as a, in comparison
Daisy is the girl in the song Daisy Bell, on a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: Lively and impudent, like the girl on the tandem in a famous song.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Bell is an old music-hall song about 'a bicycle built for two', i.e. a tandem.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone lively and full of vigour, not tired at all.

clue.text: Crunch mutton from the butcher

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Meat carved and sold at the butcher's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' is a verb here, rearranging MUTTON FROM THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The crunch is the decisive point at which something must be faced, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: One from half the pack gets a dismissal

definitions.meaning: a playing card of the red suits, hearts or diamonds, which make up half a deck
in football a referee shows this to send a player off

explanation.surface: Drawing a card from the deck gets a player sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee's sending-off is shown by holding up this card, while a heart or diamond is literally one of the cards.

clue.text: Chinese chairman takes on the rest in rebellion to become leader

indicators.note: takes on means admits within itself, so the chairman wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Chairman Mao led China

indicators.note: in rebellion suggests disorder, so the letters of rest are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mao rises up against everyone else to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes on' looks like challenging a rival, but it means holding letters inside; 'leader' here is the conductor of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor leads an orchestra, so a great musician directing it is its leader.

clue.text: Brief details help to clarify one's outlook

definitions.meaning: a short form of specifications, the details of a design
glasses, which help one see clearly

explanation.surface: A short summary can make one's view clearer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is short for both specifications and spectacles, i.e. technical details and eyeglasses.

clue.text: Wooden feature in bits, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: something in bits is broken, not whole

explanation.surface: A piece of timber that has broken into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in timber where a knot has fallen out is a feature of the wood.

clue.text: Books and singles can be found here

definitions.text: Books and singles can be found here

parts.words: Books and singles can be found here
parts.note: books stand on a ledge, and single people unlikely to marry are said to be left there

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unmarried and past the age for courting, as well as literally on a ledge.

clue.text: Seating on a roundabout put one's back up

indicators.note: a roundabout spins round, so the letters of the words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sitting someone on a merry-go-round annoyed them.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone's back up is to make them hostile, i.e. to provoke them.

clue.text: Boil in fancy steamer

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of the words fancy steamer

explanation.surface: Bringing water to the boil in an elaborate steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: fanCY STeamer gives the answer; 'Boil' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil and a sac of fluid under the skin are both swellings, close enough to be loose synonyms.

clue.text: Finish in true satisfaction

indicators.note: in shows one word placed inside the other

parts.note: true means real
to finish is to quit

explanation.surface: Ending happily with genuine contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment or redress, the satisfaction given for a wrong or a service.

clue.text: Spots broken cane

indicators.note: broken means the letters of cane are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the letters of cane are the fodder; that the answer also reads backwards across 'broken cane' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Marks showing on a snapped walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots on the skin are pimples, the symptom of this condition.

clue.text: I've innate innocence

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'I've innate innocence (7)': no anagram indicator, and I'VE INNATE has nine letters, two more than the answer; likely misread, not confirmed by search

clue.text: Chalk opposite tip making unhappy

parts.note: chalk and cheese are proverbial opposites
to tip one's hat is to doff it

explanation.surface: Pointing chalk the other way makes someone sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As different as chalk and cheese' is a British idiom for complete opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means fed up or annoyed, i.e. discontented.

clue.text: German fellow? No he's an old Turk

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Is that man German? No, he is a historic Turk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the old Turkish state, so a subject of it was a Turk of former times.

clue.text: A police department has to examine crucial trial

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
to examine is to test

explanation.surface: Detectives must check things out in a vital experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a test of gold with nitric acid, the phrase now means any decisive test.

clue.text: It is passed on the way to the Forth say

definitions.text: It is passed on the way to the Forth say

parts.words: It is passed on the way to the Forth say
parts.note: Forth sounds like fourth, so on the way from first through the numbers you pass the one just before it

explanation.definitionFit: Counting up, the ordinal before fourth must be passed, reading Forth as fourth.

clue.text: Golf club without head is still complete

indicators.note: without head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club that has lost its head still counts as whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' of a golf club suggests the club's end, but here it is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means total or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Cut by a well dressed person

definitions.text: Cut by a well dressed person

parts.words: Cut by a well dressed person
parts.note: a smart dresser is said to cut a fine figure; the word after cut in that idiom is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a dash means looking stylish, so it is what a smart person cuts.

clue.text: Unable to produce issue that's clean!

definitions.meaning: issue means children, so this is infertile
free of germs, as in surgery

explanation.surface: A publisher that cannot bring out a magazine keeps a spotless office.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both infertile and free from bacteria, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Try a Tory leader with allure

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of the word Tory

parts.note: to allure is to tempt

explanation.surface: Have a go at a Tory leader with charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A try is an effort, an attempt to do something.

clue.text: Where you might come to a full stop

definitions.text: Where you might come to a full stop

parts.words: Where you might come to a full stop
parts.note: a railway terminus where trains stop for good, or the final point of a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: The terminus of a railway route is where travel finally halts.
